wiki_and_history.briefHistory: Founded in 1871 as Alcorn University, it is the oldest public historically black land-grant institution in the United States.
famousFirsts: First black land-grant institution in the nation.
Hiram R. Revels, the first African American to serve in the U.S. Senate, was its first president.
wiki_and_history.architectureStyle: A mix of historic brick landmarks and modern athletic facilities.
funFacts: The campus is located on 1,700 acres of land in rural Claiborne County.
The school was originally named after Mississippi Governor James L. Alcorn.
